patients.summary: Construction site supervisor with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity and sleep apnea on CPAP who joined in 2023 and quit smoking in 2024. In June 2026 a high-speed car crash brought a venous air embolism after an upright central line, operative fixation of multiple orthopedic injuries and flaccid lower-limb weakness with lost lean mass; he is home after rehab, recovering, with hospital records only partly received.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is moving his primary care here; his employer plan now covers the membership. Has diabetes and BP, takes 4 meds. Wants a long first visit because he works early site hours. Booked new patient appt 9/12 at 7:30 am. Mailed intake packet and records release form; he will drop the release off this week.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications
conditions.note: Diagnosed at prior practice; metformin since.

conditions.label: Obstructive sleep apnea
conditions.note: Home sleep test at prior practice; nightly CPAP.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
38 y/o man, site supervisor for a commercial builder, here to set up primary care. Previous PCP retired and he let things drift for about a year but kept getting his refills.

Diabetes since roughly 2019, picked up on routine labs. On metformin 1000 twice a day, tolerates it, occasional loose stool if he skips breakfast. Checks sugars rarely. Last A1c he remembers was 'in the sevens'. No hypoglycemia, no foot numbness, no vision change.

BP high since about 2018, lisinopril 20 since then. No home cuff. No headaches, chest pain or swelling.

OSA dx on a home sleep test at the old practice around 2021. Uses CPAP most nights, feels better rested when he does. Mask fits fine.

Also atorvastatin 40 at bedtime and baby aspirin daily, both started by the prior PCP.

PMH: as above, plus weight (BMI around 34 for years).
PSH: tonsils out age 7. Left ankle ORIF at 32, healed, no hardware problems.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, ASA 81 daily.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: father had an MI at 58. Mother has type 2 DM. One brother with HTN.
SH: smokes, about half a pack a day, roughly 8 pack-years total. Has thought about quitting, not ready to set a date. Beer on weekends, 2-3 a week. Single, lives alone. Long days outdoors on job sites.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Heavyset, comfortable. Neck thick, no thyromegaly. Heart: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abd obese, soft, nontender. Ext: no edema, healed left ankle scars. Feet: skin intact, no calluses, monofilament felt at all sites, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. T2DM: continue metformin. A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today.
2. HTN: reasonable on lisinopril 20; recheck at follow-up.
3. Lipids/CV risk: continue atorvastatin 40. Lipid panel today. Continue aspirin as he has been taking.
4. Obesity: talked about portion size and the gas-station breakfasts on site. He is open to it.
5. OSA: keep using CPAP nightly.
6. Tobacco: advised to quit; offered support whenever he is ready, he will think on it.
7. Health maintenance: Tdap today. HCV and HIV screening once, he agreed. PHQ-2 negative. AUDIT-C 2.
8. Records request to prior practice.
Return about 4 months, or sooner by message.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Signed release on file. Request sent to prior primary care office for last 3 years of notes, labs, immunizations and sleep study.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Henry, your labs are back. A1c is 7.4, a little above where I'd like it (under 7), but not far off. Kidney and liver tests are normal, no protein in the urine, cholesterol is well controlled on the atorvastatin. Hep C and HIV screens negative. No medication changes for now; the eating changes we talked about should help. See you in January.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records from prior primary care office, 2020 to 2022, received and scanned.

Problem list: type 2 diabetes mellitus, essential hypertension, obesity, obstructive sleep apnea.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Sleep: home sleep apnea test early 2021 consistent with obstructive sleep apnea; auto-CPAP ordered through a home equipment supplier, compliance download acceptable.
Labs on file: yearly A1c in the 7 range, normal kidney function, no microalbuminuria.
Immunizations: influenza most years; COVID primary series 2021.
Reviewed by PCP; nothing new.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after work. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Flu L arm, COVID R arm, PCV20 L arm (indicated with diabetes, per PCP). VIS sheets given. Observed 15 min, felt fine, left.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM/HTN f/u. Winter is slow at work so he has been eating at home more. No lows. Taking everything daily, CPAP most nights. Still smoking, down a little, maybe 7-8 a day. Not ready for a quit date; did not want a patch.

Vitals as charted.
CV RRR. Lungs clear. Feet warm, skin intact.

A/P
T2DM: A1c drawn today, continue metformin. Walking at lunch encouraged.
HTN: slightly above goal today, he had coffee and a cigarette in the truck before coming in. Keep lisinopril 20, recheck next visit.
Tobacco: brief counseling again, door open.
RTC 6 mo.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c came down to 7.2, nice work. Kidney function and potassium fine. Same plan.

documents.title: RE: A1c result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks doc. Ill keep at it

documents.title: 90-day refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax asking to convert metformin, lisinopril and atorvastatin to 90-day supplies for his mail-order benefit. Last visit 1/10, labs current. Sent 90-day scripts with 3 refills per PCP protocol.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Dilated diabetic eye examination, 2024-04-19.
Visual acuity corrected 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS. Pupils normal. Pressures normal both eyes. Lens clear. Fundus: optic discs healthy, vessels normal caliber, no hemorrhages, exudates or microaneurysms either eye.
Impression: type 2 diabetes without diabetic retinopathy.
Recommend repeat dilated exam in 12 months.
Allergies: none known.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Did not arrive for 7:30 BP recheck. Left voicemail. Texted back that a concrete pour got moved up and he forgot to cancel. Will rebook for July with the diabetes visit.

conditions.label: History of tobacco dependence
conditions.note: Quit cigarettes June 2024, unassisted; about 8 pack-years.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Big news: stopped smoking about 5 weeks ago, cold turkey, on June 10. Said he was tired of spending the money and smelling like it. Some cravings at the end of the day, chews gum, no nicotine products. No weight gain so far.

Diabetes: feels good. Packing lunch most days. CPAP nightly. Meds without issue.

Vitals as charted, BP better today.
Heart regular. Lungs clear, no wheeze. No edema.

A/P
Tobacco: congratulated. Moved to former smoker, 8 pack-years. Talked through triggers. He declined any medication help, will message if cravings get worse.
T2DM: A1c today. Continue metformin.
HTN: at goal, lisinopril 20.
Physical in the fall with fasting labs and flu shot.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 39 y/o. Still off cigarettes, about 3.5 months now. Gained a little, expected. Busy season at work, long hours. Sleeping well with CPAP. No chest pain with exertion, no shortness of breath climbing ladders or stairs. No urinary symptoms. Mood good.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40 qhs, aspirin 81. NKDA.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT: TMs and oropharynx normal. Neck supple, no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Skin: no worrisome lesions. Ext: no edema. Diabetic foot exam: monofilament intact bilaterally, pulses good, no skin breakdown.

Screens: PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
- T2DM: A1c, microalbumin, CMP today.
- HTN, hyperlipidemia risk: lipids today, same meds.
- Former smoker: keep it up. Not a lung screening candidate at 8 pack-years and his age.
- OSA: on CPAP.
- Vaccines: flu today. Starting hepatitis B series given diabetes (2-dose), first dose today, second in a month with his COVID shot.
- Colon screening starts at 45.
Otherwise see me in about 5 months.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Henry, everything from Friday looks fine. A1c is holding right around 7, cholesterol at goal, kidney and liver tests normal, blood counts normal, urine protein negative. Nothing to change. Nurse visit for hep B #2 and COVID in about 4 weeks.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep B second dose L deltoid, completes the 2-dose series. COVID updated vaccine R deltoid. Mild arm soreness last time only. Tolerated well, waited 15 minutes.

documents.title: CPAP supplies paperwork
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Home equipment supplier called: needs a signed order and a recent note documenting CPAP use to keep shipping masks, cushions and filters. Faxed the 9/27 physical note and the signed supply order after PCP signature. Supplier confirmed receipt.
